corrections: Legacy timing checks now use authored 450 ms wind-up and 400 ms recovery.
The Signal Breach route must deal with a scout responding to a nearby fighter, instead of ignoring it during a slow survey lap.
The direct controller engages from doorway cover rather than flying onto a pursuing fighter and waiting for an enemy that was already rammed.
The fighter drill clears the responding second guard before taking the four-room survey lap.
If the scout starts outside the report radius, the Signal Breach controller enters the hall to reveal it before waiting for its wind-up.
The direct Crossfire controller prioritizes the ranged guard from doorway cover before aiming at the approaching scout.
